results.question_restated: For the ATF DNA report (State's Exhibit 30) as read into the preliminary-hearing record: what likelihood ratio is stated for the calculation that covers the rifle stock/grips together with the bolt, what are the two competing propositions in full, and which sub-item numbers does it cover?
results.finding:
REBUILT from the primary read-in. On preliminary-hearing Day 4, State's Exhibit 30 — identified by the witness as "the ATF report that I received regarding the DNA testing on the gun and cartridge and cartridge casings, oh, sorry, correction, cartridge case and cartridges" (day4.txt 05:18:35) and admitted at 05:19:32 — was taken through paragraph by paragraph. At page 5, "this first paragraph here under Statistical Analysis," counsel asked about "Exhibits 1.1 and 1.4," and the witness identified them: "Yep. They're referring to 1.1 is swabs of the stock and grips of the rifle. And then 1.4 is swabs of the bolt of the rifle with possible ridge detail and/or smudging." (day4.txt 05:21:40)

Counsel then asked him to read Paragraph D, and he read it verbatim (day4.txt 05:21:57):

"The DNA profiles are at least one trillion times more likely if they originated from Tyler Robinson, Exhibit 7.1, as a contributor to the major components and three unrelated, unknown individuals than if they originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals."

Counsel confirmed the coverage immediately after: "And again, that's swabs of the stock and grips and bolt, is that right?" — "Yes." (05:22:14–05:22:19)

THE TWO COMPETING PROPOSITIONS, IN FULL, exactly as read:
- Prosecution proposition (numerator): the DNA profiles "originated from Tyler Robinson, Exhibit 7.1, as a contributor to the major components and three unrelated, unknown individuals" — i.e. a four-person mixture in which Robinson is *a* contributor to the major components.
- Defence/alternative proposition (denominator): the DNA profiles "originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals" — a four-person mixture with no named contributor.
Exhibit 7.1 is Robinson's reference sample; 7.1 also appears in the clerk's exhibit roll-call at day4.txt ≈06:13.

SUB-ITEMS COVERED: ATF sub-items 1.1 (swabs of the stock and grips of the rifle) and 1.4 (swabs of the bolt of the rifle with possible ridge detail and/or smudging) — two swabs grouped into ONE calculation. NO separate likelihood ratio for the bolt alone, or for the stock/grips alone, exists on this record.

CALCULATION NUMBER — stated only by position, not by number, for this one. The transcript calls it "this first paragraph here under Statistical Analysis" on page 5; the next item read is expressly "Calculation number 2, ... Exhibit 1.2 ... swabs of the butt plate" (05:22:20–05:22:25), then "Calculation number 3, Exhibit 1.3" (05:22:49), "Calculation number 4, Exhibits 1.5 and 5.1" (05:23:19), "number 5, 1.6 and 3.1" (05:24:03), "Calculation number 6, Exhibit 1.9" (05:24:41), and "Number 7 ... the last one in this report" (05:25:20). So Calculation 1 = 1.1 + 1.4 by the report's own sequence; the record does not utter the label "Calculation number 1" for it. (Day 5 does not corroborate the numbering: the report's author, ATF forensic biologist Caitlin Oliver, numbered only calculation 3 (Ex. 1.3) and calculation 7 (Ex. 1.13 + 2.1) — day5.txt 02:13:23, 02:15:58.)

THE VALUE IS A FLOOR, NOT A POINT ESTIMATE. Oliver, the report's author, on Day 5 (01:38:31): "So, for our likelihood ratio statistics, we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher," and (02:15:01) "Correct. We would not report a number higher than one trillion." "At least" is therefore load-bearing.

WHAT THE PHRASING DOES NOT SAY. Calculation 1's proposition conditions Robinson as "a contributor to the major componentS" (plural, indefinite article) — not as the sole major contributor. Oliver confirmed on cross that item 1.1 alone "was a mixture of four individuals. There were two major contributors" (day5.txt 02:21:18), and the identity of the second is not on this record. Separately, for item 1.4 (the bolt) she testified: "I would say there was support for inclusion of Matthew Robinson on the sample obtained from the swabs of the bolts of the rifle" (day5.txt 01:49:41) — a named elimination-sample donor associated with the residence, not a suspect. Item 1.4 was also entirely consumed in the analysis (day5.txt 01:31:39 lists 1.4 among the consumed exhibits).

ACCESS PATH: the ATF DNA report itself (State's Exhibit 30) is NOT among the 64 banked .txt / 58 banked PDF artifacts — searched and confirmed null (see method). The four banked atf_page-*.png files are a DIFFERENT ATF report: rendering atf_page-26.png shows "BUREAU OF ALCOHOL, TOBACCO, FIREARMS AND EXPLOSIVES / Forensic Science Laboratory – Washington", "Date of Report: September 17, 2025", "Case Number: 2025-W-000401", "Type of Exam: Firearms", "Page 1 of 4". So this figure is reachable only through the courtroom reading of the document, on Rev machine transcripts — a read-aloud of a primary document, not a direct read of the filing.
results.value: at least one trillion (≥ 1 × 10^12) times more likely — a capped/floor value (ATF reporting cap = 1 trillion)
results.unit: dimensionless likelihood ratio ("times more likely"); ATF reports it capped at one trillion, with a verbal-scale equivalent above 1,000,000 = "very strong support for inclusion" (verbal scale described at day2.txt 07:18:14–07:18:42)
results.denominator: No population denominator — a likelihood ratio is a ratio of two conditional probabilities of the observed DNA profiles under two stated propositions, not a rate over a population. The "population" terms live inside the propositions: 3 vs 4 "unrelated, unknown individuals" (i.e. a four-person mixture either way, with Robinson replacing one unknown). The companion population-framed statistic (Paragraph E: "the probability of an unrelated individual in the population who has not contributed DNA to the sample yielding this level of support is less than one in a trillion") was read into the record for calculations 3 and 7 only (day5.txt 02:15:27, 02:17:56) — Paragraph E for THIS calculation was never read.
results.time_window: Read into the record on preliminary-hearing Day 4, transcript timestamp 05:21:57 (Rev page dated July 10, 2026; Days 1–5 Rev pages dated July 7, 8, 9, 10 and 13, 2026). Restated in the State's closing argument at the 2026-09-01 hearing (Rev page dated September 2, 2026). The ATF DNA report's own date of report and testing dates were NOT read into the record in this passage; the swabs derive from the 2025-09-10 rifle recovery and subsequent submissions.
results.comparator: The alternative (defence) proposition inside the same sentence: "than if they originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals." Within-report comparators read on the same page range: butt plate (1.2) and trigger/trigger guard (1.3) also "at least one trillion"; fore-end+cartridge (1.5+5.1) and barrel+cartridge (1.6+3.1) also "at least one trillion"; optical accessory (1.9) "6.28 billion times more likely" — the only sub-cap, uncapped point value read that day (day4.txt 05:25:04).

(1) PRIMARY READ-IN — day4.txt ( 05:21:57 ), Sgt. Faumuina reading Paragraph D verbatim from State's Exhibit 30:

results.breaks:
SEVEN P8 breaks actually observed:

1. CENSORED VALUE PRESENTED AS A NUMBER (stock-vs-flow analogue: a floor vs a point estimate). "At least one trillion" is a reporting cap, not a computed value: "for our likelihood ratio statistics, we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher" (day5.txt 01:38:31); "We would not report a number higher than one trillion" (02:15:01). Any arithmetic on "1 trillion" treats a censored floor as a measurement. The State's own argument then does exactly that at 2026-09-01 ( 06:22:25 ): "To give context to that likelihood, to that 1 trillion number, our world population is approximately 8.3 billion people. To equal a trillion would require replicating our world with the current population 120.48 times" — a population-scaling gloss applied to a cap.

2. GROUPED ITEMS, NO PER-ITEM VALUE (n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another). Calculation 1 covers 1.1 AND 1.4 together. Lifting it as "the bolt LR" or "the stock LR" invents a per-item figure the record does not contain. Oliver confirmed the grouping rule is results-based, not batch-based, for the analogous calc 7: "They were both mixtures of two individuals and they both yielded a likelihood ratio of the same magnitude so they can be grouped together" — "It's not that they were tested together?" — "Correct." (day5.txt 02:17:08–02:17:23).

3. IDENTICAL HEADLINE NUMBER, DIFFERENT PROPOSITIONS — not like-for-like. Across State's Exhibit 30 the same "at least one trillion" attaches to calculations with different mixture sizes: calc 1 (1.1+1.4) = Robinson + 3 unknowns vs 4 unknowns; calc 2 (butt plate) = Robinson + 4 vs 5; calc 3 (trigger) = Robinson + 3 vs 4; calc 4 and 5 = Robinson + 2 vs 3; calc 7 = Robinson + 1 vs 2. Same number, different denominators of the underlying comparison.

4. CAPPED FLOOR COMPARED AGAINST AN UNCAPPED POINT VALUE. The optical accessory (1.9) is "6.28 billion times more likely" (day4.txt 05:25:04) — a real computed value. Ranking it against the capped "at least one trillion" items compares two different kinds of quantity.

5. TWO OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS OF "MAJOR" IN THE SAME REPORT, plus a third in argument. "a contributor to the major components" (calc 1, 5) vs "the major component" (calc 2, 3) vs "the major components" (calc 4) vs "the major contributor" (day5 calc 7) vs the State's "a major contributor" (2026-09-01 08:08:34). Calc 1 uses the weakest form, and item 1.1 independently had TWO major contributors in a four-person mixture (day5.txt 02:21:18) — so "a contributor to the major components" cannot be read as sole-source language.

6. POPULATION-DEFINITION TENSION WITHIN THE SAME REPORT, unreconciled on the record. Calculation 1's propositions are framed entirely in terms of "unrelated, unknown individuals," while the report's own item-level results for one of the two grouped swabs report "support for inclusion of Matthew Robinson on the sample obtained from the swabs of the bolts of the rifle" (day5.txt 01:49:41) — a named, RELATED elimination donor. Two sections of one report using different operational frames for who the non-Robinson contributors could be. I record the tension; I do not resolve it, and nothing here implies anyone is a suspect.

7. CALCULATION NUMBER IS POSITIONAL, NOT STATED. "Calculation 1" for 1.1+1.4 is derived from Day 4's sequence (the next paragraph is expressly "Calculation number 2"); the label is never spoken for this paragraph, and Day 5 numbers only calculations 3 and 7. Single-day, single-source numbering.

Also noted, not a break in the figure itself: both sources are Rev MACHINE transcripts; the Day-4 speaker labels are the known-unreliable kind (a "Ms. Visser" label appears mid-Faumuina exchange at day5.txt 02:08:12 where the answer is plainly the witness's), so speakers were inferred from content, not labels. The number and both propositions sit inside a single continuous read-aloud and are unaffected.

results.question_restated: For the ATF DNA report calculation covering the rifle's butt plate, what likelihood ratio does the record state, with both propositions (numerator and denominator) in full and the sub-item (exhibit) number?
results.finding:
ESTABLISHED FROM THE PRIMARY RECORD (sworn testimony reading the report aloud; the report itself is not in the bank).

The butt-plate calculation is **Statistical Analysis Calculation number 2** of **State's Exhibit 30 (the ATF DNA report on the rifle and its ammunition)**, page 5, paragraph D, and it covers **ATF sub-item / Exhibit 1.2**.

Sub-item identification, verbatim (day4.txt):
Mr. McBride ( 05:22:20 ): "Okay. Number 2, Calculation number 2, where is this swab taken from?"
Sergeant Faumuina ( 05:22:25 ): "Exhibit 1.2 would be swabs of the butt plate of the rifle."

The figure, verbatim, as read into the record by Sgt. Faumuina from paragraph D (day4.txt):
Mr. McBride ( 05:22:30 ): "And will you read Paragraph D here?"
Sergeant Faumuina ( 05:22:33 ): **"The DNA profile is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a major component and four unrelated, unknown individuals than if it originated from five unrelated, unknown individuals."**

Both propositions in full:
- **H1 (numerator / prosecution proposition):** the DNA profile from the Exhibit 1.2 butt-plate swabs originated from **Tyler Robinson as a major component and four unrelated, unknown individuals** (5 contributors, one of them Robinson).
- **H2 (denominator / alternative proposition):** the same profile originated from **five unrelated, unknown individuals** (5 contributors, none of them Robinson).
- **LR ≥ 1,000,000,000,000 (1 × 10^12)** — stated as "at least one trillion times more likely."

Corroborating primary testimony on the same sub-item, from the report's author (day5.txt, ATF DNA Section Chief Caitlin Oliver, examined by defense counsel Michael Burt):
- ( 02:04:37–02:05:08 ) Burt: "…with regard to the 1.2 sample, 'The profile consistent with at least five contributors, at least one of which is male,'" — Oliver: "Correct." (This fixes the mixture size underlying both propositions: 5.)
- ( 01:19:42 ) Burt: "the next sample down, 1.2, where the state read paragraph D, admitted paragraph F, you state in F, based on this calculation, there is evidentiary support for the inclusion of Tyler Robinson, correct? As a possible contributor." — Oliver: "Correct." (Paragraph F of the same 1.2 calculation; Burt directs the display "back to that page please, five.")
- ( 02:14:51–02:15:06 ) The "at least one trillion" is a **reporting ceiling, not a measured value**: McBride: "…the protocols in your laboratory say you cap that at the number one trillion. Is that right?" — Oliver: "Correct. We would not report a number higher than one trillion."

⚠ The ATF DNA report itself (State's Exhibit 30) is **not among the banked artifacts**. The four banked `atf_page-26..29.png` renders are a *different* ATF report — "Type of Exam: Firearms," Case Number 2025-W-000401, dated September 17, 2025, "Page 1 of 4" (the firearms/toolmark report, State's Exhibit 32). So the butt-plate figure is reachable only as read aloud into the record by witnesses; it is Tier 1 as to what the witnesses said, and is **T1-via-testimony as to the document**, which this project has not read.

results.unit: dimensionless likelihood ratio — ratio of the probability of the observed DNA profile under H1 to its probability under H2; verbalized in the report as "times more likely." Value is left-censored at the lab's 1-trillion reporting cap ("at least").
results.denominator: Denominator proposition (H2): the profile originated from **five unrelated, unknown individuals**. Population/sample: the DNA profile developed from ATF Exhibit **1.2** — "swabs of the butt plate of the rifle" (the Exhibit 1 Mauser model 98, .30-06 Springfield rifle, s/n 8863) — a profile the analyst's report describes as "consistent with at least five contributors, at least one of which is male" (day5.txt 02:05:08). The reference population is "unrelated, unknown individuals"; no population database, ethnicity panel or allele-frequency set was named in anything read into the record.

FIVE P8 breaks actually observed in the record:

1. **CENSORED VALUE PRESENTED AS A MAGNITUDE (crude vs adjusted / ceiling effect).** "At least one trillion" is a **lab reporting cap**, not a computed result: "the protocols in your laboratory say you cap that at the number one trillion" — "Correct. Any arithmetic on 1e12 — averaging, multiplying across items, world-population analogies — is arithmetic on a ceiling. The State's closing does exactly that: "To equal a trillion would require replicating our world with the current population 120.48 times" (2026-09-01, 06:22:25), a precision computed from a censored bound.

2. **SAME HEADLINE NUMBER, DIFFERENT DENOMINATORS (operational-definition swap).** Six of the seven calculations all read "at least 1 trillion," but each conditions on a *different* contributor structure: butt plate 4-vs-5 unknowns, stock/grips+bolt 3-vs-4, trigger 3-vs-4, fore-end+cartridge 2-vs-3, receiver underside+case 1-vs-2. The butt plate's "1 trillion" and the receiver's "1 trillion" are **not the same quantity** and are not comparable, poolable or multipliable. The repeated "Again, 1 trillion times more likely" in closing (06:20:38 et seq.) flattens six distinct propositions into one apparent number.

3. **n-IN-ONE-PLACE ≠ n-IN-ANOTHER (calculations vs items).** There are **7 statistical calculations** but **11+ exhibit sub-items**, because several calculations group two items (1.1+1.4; 1.5+5.1; 1.6+3.1; 1.13+2.1). Oliver: they were grouped because "they both yielded a likelihood ratio of the same magnitude so they can be grouped together," explicitly **not** because they were tested together (day5.txt 02:17:08–02:17:29). Counting "seven calculations" as seven items, or treating a grouped calculation as one sample, both misstate the denominator. Item 1.2 (butt plate) is a single-item calculation — no grouping.

4. **THE DENOMINATOR'S CONTRIBUTOR COUNT IS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT — and the record diverges on whether it moves the figure.** The 1.2 profile is "consistent with **at least** five contributors"; Oliver agreed "at least" signals it could be more (day5.txt 02:05:08). Her own SOP (Exhibit Oliver 148, p. 83) states "approximately 70% of four-person mixtures present as two- or three-person mixtures based solely on number of alleles present," which she confirmed (02:06:21–02:08:12). Asked whether the final LR depends on the assumed number of contributors, she answered "**No, it does not**" (02:04:04) and then, four seconds later, "**It can have an effect. It's possible**" (02:04:08). That is an unreconciled statement about the statistic's own sensitivity to its denominator, on the record, from its author.

5. **STOCK vs FLOW / WHAT THE RATIO IS ABOUT.** The LR is a ratio of probabilities **of the evidence given two propositions**, not a probability that Robinson touched the butt plate, and not a random-match probability — Oliver: paragraph E "itself is not a random match probability statistic. It is a way to represent the likelihood ratio similar to a random match probability" (day5.txt 02:21:57); "we can't do a source attribution" (02:22:32); and there is "no way of knowing when or how the DNA got on those samples" (02:21:24–02:21:37). Separately, for item 1.2 only paragraphs D and F were read into the record — **the paragraph-E probability restatement for the butt plate was never read**, so the "less than one in a trillion" phrasing quoted at 02:15:27 belongs to calculation 3, not calculation 2, and must not be transferred.

PLUS an access-path break, not a P8 category but load-bearing: **the source document is unbanked.** State's Exhibit 30 exists in this record only as read aloud. The four banked ATF page renders are the *Firearms* report (2025-W-000401). Defense counsel put the selectivity of that reading in issue on the record: the State "selectively read into the record a portion of those reports, which left an extremely misleading impression of the significance of that evidence" (day5.txt 01:12:xx, Burt). The figure above is therefore solid as to **what was said under oath** and unverified as to **what the document says in full.**

results.question_restated: For the ATF DNA report's statistical-analysis calculation No. 3 — Exhibit 1.3, the swabs of the trigger and trigger guard of the rifle — what likelihood ratio does the record state, how many contributors was that sample said to have, and what does the record say about degradation and about the two surfaces having been swabbed together?
results.finding:
The record states the figure three times, in three different mouths, and all three agree on magnitude: **at least one trillion**, as a capped floor rather than a point estimate.

1. **Verbatim read-in of the report's own Paragraph D** (Day 4, Sgt. Faumuina reading State's Exhibit 30 aloud at counsel's direction). McBride: "Looking at Calculation number 3, Exhibit 1.3, what areas were swabbed for this comparison?" Faumuina (05:22:56): "1.3 is swabs of the trigger and trigger guard of the rifle with possible ridge detail and/or smudging." McBride: "Will you read Paragraph D?" Faumuina (05:23:05): "**The DNA profile is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a major component and three unrelated, unknown individuals than if it originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals.**"

2. **The report's author, under oath** — Caitlin Oliver, "DNA Section Chief" at "the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives" (day5.txt 01:14:59), who received the case "on September 12th, 2025" (01:28:54). She first identified the exhibit (02:13:56): "1.3 is the swabs of the trigger and trigger guard of the rifle." Then (02:14:27): "**For this exhibit, the DNA profile was at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as the major component and three unknown unrelated individuals than if it originated from four unrelated individuals.**"

3. **State's closing argument** (Mr. Grunander, 2026-09-01, 06:20:38), reading from "State's Exhibit 30, this is the ATF report": "The trigger, the actual trigger to the gun and the trigger guard of the rifle, **the DNA profile is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as the major component and three unrelated unknown individuals than if it originated from four unrelated unknown individuals.** Again, 1 trillion times more likely."

**The one trillion is a reporting cap, not a result.** Oliver (day5.txt 01:38:31): "So, for our likelihood ratio statistics, **we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher**." And on this calculation specifically — McBride (02:14:45): "You say at least one trillion times more likely. So it could be a much higher number than one trillion. Is that accurate?" Oliver (02:14:51): "It's possible." McBride (02:14:54): "But the protocols in your laboratory say you cap that at the number one trillion. Is that right?" Oliver (02:15:01): "Correct. **We would not report a number higher than one trillion.**"

**The companion statistic (Paragraph E) for the same calculation** (day5.txt 02:15:27): "**The probability of an unrelated individual in the population who has not contributed DNA to the sample yielding this level of support is less than one in a trillion.**" Oliver characterised it (02:15:13) as "another way of stating the likelihood ratio statistic," and later (02:21:57) declined to call it a random match probability: "It itself is not a random match probability statistic. It is a way to represent the likelihood ratio similar to a random match probability." It is capped the same way (02:15:55, "Correct").

**CONTRIBUTORS — four in the calculation, "at least four" in the profile description, open-ended on cross.** The LR's numerator proposition assumes exactly four people (Robinson + three unknown); the denominator proposition assumes four unrelated unknowns. But the report's characterisation of the profile is a floor, not a fixed n. Burt (day5.txt 02:19:07): "And you said with regard to that sample that that was a sample consistent with **at least four contributors**, right?" Oliver (02:19:19): "Correct. Correct." Burt (02:19:47): "You can't tell us anything about whether when you say it's at least four, **it could be five, six, or seven people** with DNA on that trigger or trigger guard, correct?" Oliver (02:20:00): "Correct. Which is why we have the major contributor that is suitable for comparison and the minor contributor is not suitable for comparison due to that complexity." On the "at least" convention generally, Burt (02:04:37) quoted her report's language for other items ("The profile is consistent with at least four contributors") and asked, "I assume by the word at least you're signaling that it could be more." Oliver (02:05:08): "Correct." She also agreed (01:38:15 context) with the NIST caveat that "The true number of contributors of DNA to an item can never be known," and told the court (02:04:04) the final LR does "not" depend on the assumed number of contributors, immediately qualifying (02:04:08): "It can have an effect. It's possible."

**DEGRADATION — present in this sample, and worst in the major profile.** Burt (day5.txt 02:18:59): "And that's one of the samples that was degraded, correct?" Oliver (02:19:04): "**There were signs of degradation present in that sample, yes.**" Burt (02:19:21): "And did what you termed the major profile have the largest amount of degradation in that sample?" Oliver (02:19:32): "**There was... Yes.**" (The major profile is the one compared to Robinson.) Generally, Oliver (01:45:43): "There was degradation present in some of the samples," causes being "environmental insults, heat, humidity."

**SWABBED TOGETHER — yes, and the analyst cannot say which surface the DNA came from.** Burt (day5.txt 02:18:30): "The 1.3 sample is described as swabs of trigger and trigger guard, right?" Oliver (02:18:38): "Correct." Burt (02:18:39): "You didn't do the swabs, but am I correct that you have no way of knowing which part was from the trigger and which part was from the trigger guard?" Oliver (02:18:53): "**Correct. So they were swabbed together, so I wouldn't be able to say where the DNA came from.**" She did not take the swabs herself (02:16:35, "I did not"). She also could not date the deposit — Burt (02:19:38): "And you can't tell us anything about when the DNA was deposited on the trigger guard or the trigger, correct?" Oliver (02:19:46): "Correct." And on secondary transfer to a trigger specifically (01:45:05), asked whether a handshake could put another person's DNA on a trigger she then touched: "It is possible, yes."

**Context for "major":** Burt (02:20:10) established that "major/minor just has to do with the levels of DNA you were seeing. It has nothing to do with someone being engaged in activity that is major"; Oliver (02:20:23): "Yes. So the major contributor is the majority of the DNA contributed to that sample."

**ACCESS-PATH CAVEAT.** The ATF DNA report itself (State's Exhibit 30) is **not** among the banked primary artifacts. The four banked ATF page images are a different document — I rendered atf_page-26.png and it is the ATF Forensic Science Laboratory–Washington report, Case Number 2025-W-000401, Date of Report September 17, 2025, "Type of Exam: Firearms" (toolmarks), page 1 of 4. So the figure is established from sworn testimony that reads and quotes the DNA report — including from its author — not from direct reading of the filing itself.

Across labs, the FBI report (State's Exhibit 31) gave "1.7 octillion" for the towel and "30 quintillion" for the screwdriver (2026-09-01 06:17:24–06:19:27) — figures far above the ATF cap, from a different laboratory operating under different reporting rules. Oliver's verbal scale: an LR ≥ one million is "very strong support for inclusion"; an LR of two is the threshold for "even limited support" (day2.txt 07:18:42, 07:19:01 — Bakker's parallel scale).

results.breaks:
Observed, not hypothesised:
1. CENSORED/TRUNCATED STATISTIC REPORTED AS A MAGNITUDE. "At least one trillion" is a lab-imposed ceiling ("we cap the statistic at one trillion"; "We would not report a number higher than one trillion"). The true LR is unknown and unbounded above. Any use of this as a point value, or any ranking of ATF items against each other, is invalid — six of the seven ATF calculations read into the record sit at the identical capped value and are therefore not distinguishable from one another.
2. TWO SOURCES, DIFFERENT OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS. The FBI figures in the same closing (1.7 octillion, 30 quintillion) are uncapped; the ATF figures are capped at 1e12. Comparing them — as the closing argument does, explicitly ranking "octillion" over "trillion" — compares a raw value with a truncated one. The ATF items look weaker than the FBI items as an artefact of reporting policy, not of evidentiary strength.
3. n-IN-ONE-PLACE ≠ n-IN-ANOTHER. The LR is computed under a fixed four-person model; the same report describes the same profile as "at least four contributors," and the analyst conceded it could be five, six or seven. The statistic's denominator assumes a number the report itself declines to fix. Oliver additionally gave two answers on whether n affects the LR: "No, it does not" (02:04:04), then "It can have an effect. It's possible" (02:04:08). Her own SOP, as read to her, warns that "approximately 70% of four-person mixtures present as two- or three-person mixtures based solely on number of alleles present" (02:06:00).
4. COMPOSITE UNIT / DENOMINATOR SWAP AT RESTATEMENT. The measured unit is one swab spanning two surfaces — "they were swabbed together, so I wouldn't be able to say where the DNA came from." Downstream restatements silently narrow the unit to one surface: the Information says the DNA "was found on the rifle's trigger," and the closing calls it "the actual trigger to the gun." The figure cannot bear "on the trigger" as distinct from "on the trigger guard."
5. TRANSPOSED-CONDITIONAL HAZARD IN THE PARAGRAPH-E FORM. "Less than one in a trillion" is a restatement of the capped LR, not a random match probability — the witness said so explicitly — yet it reads as a population frequency and is equally capped, so "less than one in a trillion" is likewise a bound, not a value.
6. QUALITY CAVEAT NOT CARRIED BY THE NUMBER. Degradation was present in this sample and was heaviest in the major profile — the very profile compared to Robinson. No version of the figure, in any of its three appearances, carries that qualifier.
7. STOCK-VS-FLOW / TIMING: the statistic is a static presence measure and, by the analyst's own concession, says nothing about when or how the DNA arrived ("Correct," 02:19:46), nor does it exclude secondary transfer ("It is possible, yes," 01:45:05). Not a break in the arithmetic, but it is the boundary the number cannot cross.

results.finding:
The figure is established from the preliminary-hearing record, not from any library file. On Day 4 of the preliminary hearing (Rev transcript page-dated July 10, 2026), prosecutor Ryan McBride walked Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina through State's Exhibit 30 — identified by her at 05:18:35 as "the ATF report that I received regarding the DNA testing on the gun and cartridge and cartridge casings, oh, sorry, correction, cartridge case and cartridges," admitted by Judge Graf at 05:19:32 — calculation by calculation, having her read Paragraph D of each aloud.

SUB-ITEMS. McBride, 05:24:03: "All right. Let's look at Calculation number 5, 1.6 and 3.1. What are those?" Faumuina, 05:24:09: "1.6 is swabs of the barrel of the rifle with possible ridge detail and/or smudging. And 3.1 is swabs of one .30-06 cartridge." McBride, 05:24:19: "And that .30-06 cartridge came from where?" Faumuina, 05:24:21: "From the firearm."

THE FIGURE AND BOTH PROPOSITIONS. McBride, 05:24:22: "Will you read Paragraph D?" Faumuina, 05:24:24, quoting the report verbatim: "The DNA profiles are at least one trillion times more likely if they originated from Tyler Robinson as a contributor to the major components and two unrelated, unknown individuals than if they originated from three unrelated, unknown individuals."

So: H1 (numerator proposition) = Tyler Robinson as a contributor to the major components + two unrelated, unknown individuals (three contributors). H2 (denominator proposition) = three unrelated, unknown individuals. LR ≥ 1×10^12.

THE VALUE IS A FLOOR, NOT A POINT ESTIMATE. The report's author, ATF forensic biologist Caitlin Oliver, testified on Day 5 that "for our likelihood ratio statistics, we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher. It could be quintillion, octillion" (day5.txt 01:38:31) and "We would not report a number higher than one trillion" (02:15:01). She also adopted, from the NIST Mixture Study, that "a likelihood ratio numeric value is not a measurement of the physical quantity" (02:03:15) and that a likelihood ratio "cannot speak to the likelihood of a proposition, only to the probability of the results" (01:41:15). The 1-trillion cap is a censoring rule, so ≥1×10^12 is the reported floor for six of the seven calculations in this report; only calculation 6 (item 1.9, the optical accessory, "6.28 billion times more likely," 05:25:04) falls below the cap and carries an uncensored value.

ONE STATISTIC, TWO PHYSICAL SAMPLES. Calculation 5 reports a single LR over two separately swabbed items. Oliver explained the grouping rule on Day 5 for the analogous calculation 7: the two items were grouped "not that they were tested together" but because "they both yielded a likelihood ratio of the same magnitude so they can be grouped together" (day5.txt 02:17:08–02:17:29). The individual LRs for 1.6 and for 3.1 are therefore not separately stated anywhere on this record.

WHAT THE RECORD DOES *NOT* CARRY FOR THIS CALCULATION. Paragraph E (the reciprocal "the probability of an unrelated individual in the population who has not contributed DNA to this sample yielding this level of support is less than one in one trillion") and Paragraph F (the "evidentiary support for the inclusion of Tyler Robinson as a possible contributor" conclusion) were read aloud for other calculations but NOT for calculation 5. Any "less than one in a trillion" attached to the barrel item would be an import from a neighbouring calculation.

BOTH SAMPLES ARE GONE. Oliver's consumption list (day5.txt 01:31:39) — "It would be exhibits 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1" — includes both 1.6 and 3.1. Neither can be re-tested or the figure re-derived from the sample.

PRIMARY-DOCUMENT STATUS. State's Exhibit 30 (the ATF DNA report) is NOT in the banked corpus; the only banked ATF report is the firearms/toolmark report (State's Exhibit 32) at pp.25–29 of tyler-robinson-ballistics-motion.pdf, which contains no DNA likelihood ratios. This figure is therefore Tier 1 sworn testimony reading a Tier 1 document verbatim into the record, not a direct read of the report. The library's own CR-E02 §5.1 and DNA-E01 tables restate the same wording identically — corroboration only; they were consulted after the transcript, not relied on.

results.breaks:
1. IDENTIFIER COLLISION — TWO DIFFERENT "CALCULATION NUMBER 5"s, BOTH ABOUT A .30-06 ITEM, BOTH "AT LEAST ONE TRILLION." Thirteen minutes later on the same day, State's Exhibit 33 (a second ATF forensic-biology report, on the Dremel tool and the safe-top cartridge cases) was walked through in the same format: McBride 05:35:20 "And Calculation number 5, 18.1?"; Faumuina 05:35:24 "This is swabs of one etched .30-06 cartridge case" (from on top of the safe, the "test shot" engraving); Paragraph D at 05:35:41: "The DNA profile is at least one trillion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a major component and two unrelated, unknown individuals than if it originated from three unrelated, unknown individuals." Same magnitude, same 2-vs-3 contributor counts, different report, different item, singular profile, and "as a major component" rather than "as a contributor to the major components." A bare citation to "ATF calculation 5" is ambiguous on this record.

2. NEAR-TWIN INSIDE THE SAME REPORT. Calculation 4 (items 1.5 fore-end + 5.1 "swabs of one .30-06 cartridge," also "From the firearm," 05:23:30–05:23:48) carries the identical value and identical contributor counts but reads "as the major components," not "as a contributor to the major components." The two cartridge sub-items are described in identical words and differ only by number (5.1 vs 3.1). Role-wording and cartridge-identity swaps between calculations 4 and 5 are near-invisible.

3. CENSORED VALUE TREATED AS A MEASUREMENT. "At least one trillion" is a floor imposed by lab policy (Oliver: "we cap the statistic at one trillion… It could be quintillion, octillion," day5 01:38:31), and Oliver adopted the NIST position that an LR "is not a measurement of the physical quantity" (day5 02:03:15). Six of the report's seven calculations sit at the identical censored value, so the calculations cannot be ranked against one another and the equality across items is an artifact of the cap, not a finding.

4. ONE FIGURE, TWO SAMPLES (n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another). The single LR covers two physically separate swabs grouped only because their results were "of the same magnitude," expressly "not that they were tested together" (day5 02:17:08–02:17:29). Quoting this number as "the barrel LR" or "the cartridge LR" over-resolves it; neither per-item value is on the record.

5. OPERATIONAL-DEFINITION SWAP — CARTRIDGE vs CARTRIDGE CASE. Item 3.1 here is a cartridge; Oliver drew the distinction explicitly: "A cartridge is unfired. Cartridge case has been fired" (day5 02:16:50). The State's closing calls the calculation-7 item "another one of the .30-06 cartridges" (2026-09-01, 06:21:35) when 2.1 is a fired cartridge CASE (day5 02:16:22). The same swap applied to calculation 5 would move the item from an unfired cartridge in the rifle to the fired case.

6. DENOMINATOR-POPULATION SCOPE. H2's population is "unrelated, unknown individuals," yet the same sub-item 1.6 separately carries, in Oliver's elimination-sample report, "support for inclusion of Matthew Robinson" — Tyler Robinson's father, an elimination donor sought because he was associated with the premises, not as a suspect (day5 01:50:13–01:50:34; cf. 01:49:41 for item 1.4). A first-degree relative lies outside the stated alternative population. Recorded as a scope observation about the denominator, adopted as an argument by nobody.

7. MISSING COMPANION PARAGRAPHS. Paragraph E (the "less than one in one trillion" reciprocal) and Paragraph F (the "evidentiary support for the inclusion" conclusion) were read for other calculations but not for calculation 5; attaching either to the barrel item would be an import.

8. PAGE LOCATOR IS INFERRED, NOT STATED. McBride said "If we can go to Page 6" before calculation 4 (05:23:19) and named no page for calculation 5. Citing "Exhibit 30 p. 6" for this figure is an inference from turn order.

Counsel then drew the distinction that makes 2.1 a FIRED item: "And what's the difference between a cartridge case and a cartridge?" — "A cartridge is unfired. Cartridge case has been fired." (02:16:46–02:16:50).

On why the two are reported as one calculation: "They were both mixtures of two individuals and they both yielded a likelihood ratio of the same magnitude so they can be grouped together" — and expressly NOT because they were tested together ("It's not that they were tested together?" — "Correct." 02:17:08–02:17:23).

THE FIGURE, verbatim (day5.txt 02:17:35): "The DNA profiles are at least one trillion times more likely if they originated from Tyler Robinson as the major contributor and an unknown unrelated individual than if they originated from two unknown unrelated individuals."

So: Hp = Tyler Robinson as the major contributor + one unknown, unrelated individual. Hd = two unknown, unrelated individuals. Sub-items = ATF 1.13 (protected underside of the receiver after disassembly) and ATF 2.1 (one fired .30-06 cartridge case). Calculation 7, State's Exhibit 30 p. 7.

THE COMPANION PARAGRAPH-E STATISTIC, same calculation, verbatim (02:17:56): "So the probability of an unrelated individual in the population who has not contributed DNA to these samples yielding this level of support, so meaning yielding this likelihood ratio, is less than one in a trillion." It is a way to represent the likelihood ratio similar to a random match probability." (02:21:57).

THE VALUE IS A CENSORED FLOOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Same witness, same day (01:38:31): "So, for our likelihood ratio statistics, we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher. It could be quintillion, octillion. We chose a trillion because it has meaning to people that can understand what a trillion is." results.breaks:
SEVEN P8 breaks observed, all in the record itself.

1. CENSORED VALUE PRESENTED AS A QUANTITY (a "rounded figure" that is really a bound). "At least one trillion" is the laboratory's reporting cap, not a computed result: "we cap the statistic at one trillion. The actual number could be a lot higher. It could be quintillion, octillion" (01:38:31). Any use of this figure as a magnitude — ranking it, averaging it, or treating equality across calculations as sameness — is invalid. Proof it is a cap rather than the result: calculation 6 / item 1.9 in the SAME report was reported at "6.28 billion" (day4.txt 05:25:04), below the cap.

2. FLOOR AND CEILING CARRYING THE SAME WORD. Calculation 7 yields BOTH "at least one trillion times more likely" (a floor on a ratio) and "less than one in a trillion" (a ceiling on a probability). Two different statistics, opposite directions, identical headline number, four sentences apart in the transcript. The witness expressly refused the random-match-probability label for the second (02:21:57), and agreed the trillion "could be far less than that" on the paragraph-E side (02:15:44–02:15:55).

3. n-IN-ONE-PLACE ≠ n-IN-ANOTHER, AT THE ITEM LEVEL — pooling. One figure covers TWO physically distinct items (1.13 and 2.1) that were NOT tested together; they were reported together only because "they both yielded a likelihood ratio of the same magnitude" (02:17:08–02:17:23). Nothing on this record states a ratio for the receiver underside ALONE. A sentence attributing ≥1 trillion to the protected underside by itself is not supported by the source, and because the pooling criterion was "same magnitude," the grouping is downstream of the numbers rather than upstream.

4. TWO SOURCES, DIFFERENT OPERATIONAL DEFINITION OF THE SAME ITEM. The witness classifies ATF 2.1 as a fired cartridge CASE and defines the term against "cartridge" (unfired) at 02:16:50; the State's closing at 06:21:35 calls the same item "another one of the .30-06 cartridges." The whole evidentiary point of item 2.1 — that it was fired — is erased by the second wording.

5. DENOMINATOR/CONTRIBUTOR-COUNT SWAP ACROSS CALCULATIONS THAT ALL READ "ONE TRILLION." Calculation 7's propositions assume a TWO-person mixture (1 + 1 unknown vs 2 unknown). Calculation 1 assumes four (Robinson + 3 vs 4), calculation 2 assumes five (Robinson + 4 vs 5), calculation 3 assumes four. Identical printed magnitude, different hypothesis pairs and different mixture complexity — the figures are not commensurable even within one report, and the shared "one trillion" is an artifact of the cap, not agreement between calculations.

6. CROSS-LABORATORY UNIT MISMATCH IN THE SAME CLOSING ARGUMENT. Minutes before reciting calculation 7, the same speaker recited FBI figures — "1.7 octillion" (towel) and "30 quintillion" (screwdriver) — whose propositions place Lance Twiggs on BOTH sides and which are stated values, not capped floors (06:17–06:19:27). The argument then supplies a scale analogy for the trillion ("replicating our world with the current population 120.48 times"). Ranking ATF's capped floor against the FBI's uncapped stated value is a category error; the record does not say whether the FBI applies a cap at all.

7. THE POOLED FIGURE IS HALF NON-RETESTABLE (stock-vs-flow analogue for the evidence base). Of the two items behind this single number, ATF 2.1 was ENTIRELY CONSUMED in the analysis and only 1.13's extract was retained (01:31:39–01:32:14). The reported quantity is therefore not reproducible from source material for half of what it covers.

TRANSCRIPT-QUALITY CAVEAT (access path, not a break in the figure): these are Rev machine transcripts. Visible garbles in the immediate neighborhood include "one 30-06 six cartridge" (02:13:04) and "the probability of scene a DNA profile" for "seeing" (day2.txt 07:11:38). Speaker attribution at 02:17:35 was confirmed from content (a witness answering her own report), not from the Rev label. The report itself — State's Exhibit 30 — is not banked, so this figure cannot presently be read off the primary document; every reading of it is a witness or an advocate reciting a page on a courtroom screen.

The witness is Caitlin Oliver, who testified "I work for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives as a DNA Section Chief" and "I've been a Section Chief since January and I've worked with the ATF for about nine years" (day5.txt, 01:14:59 and 01:15:08; name spelled on the record at 01:14:47, "Caitlin Oliver, O-L-I-V-E-R"). Day 5 of the preliminary hearing is dated July 13, 2026 on the Rev page header.

THE PAGE THEY WERE READ AGAINST. Defense counsel Michael Burt: "Okay. Could you now go back to Exhibit 30, page eight? Were certain DNA samples consumed in your analysis?" — Oliver: "Yes, they were." (01:31:08 / 01:31:28). Burt: "And for the record, are those listed on page eight of your report?" — Oliver: "Yes, they are." (01:31:29 / 01:31:34). So: page eight of State's/Plaintiff's Exhibit 30, counsel-named and witness-confirmed as her own report. Exhibit 30 had been re-displayed at 01:22:34 ("Could you re-display Exhibit 30 please?") and page eight of the same document was already in use at 01:24:33 for the DOJ ULTR language, so the page-eight reference is continuous with the displayed exhibit.

LIST 1 — ENTIRELY CONSUMED (the witness's own unaided recitation). Burt: "Which samples were entirely consumed in your analysis?" — Oliver: "It would be exhibits 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1." (01:31:35 / 01:31:39). Nine sub-items.

LIST 2 — EXTRACT RETAINED (counsel's reading of the page, assented to — NOT the witness's own recitation). Burt: "Okay. Then, are there a number of samples listed above there in the report where you say the DNA extracts will be retained? And then you list 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.13, 7.1 and 8.1?" — Oliver: "Correct." (01:31:51 / 01:32:14). Nine sub-items. Note the word "above": on the face of p. 8 the retained list sits ABOVE the consumed list.

WHAT "CONSUMED" AND "RETAINED" MEAN HERE, from the same witness. Burt: "Does that mean that these... Those are all swab samples, correct?" — Oliver: "They were swabs, yes." (01:32:15 / 01:32:20). Burt: "All right. Does your report mean that you consume the swabs, but you have some liquid extract remaining as to those samples?" — Oliver: "Correct." (01:32:21 / 01:32:32). Oliver testified she obtained permission to consume before any work began — "it's standard procedure at our laboratory that when we receive a case, we request permission to consume from the agent... we will not begin any work on the case until we've received that permission to consume" (01:29:36) — and that "Where possible, we will not consume samples where it's possible" (01:30:10), agreeing the NRC 1996 split-the-sample recommendation is a longstanding policy (01:30:26 / 01:30:46). results.breaks:
Seven P8 breaks actually observed on the record.

1. ASYMMETRIC ATTESTATION — the two lists are not of equal evidentiary quality. The consumed list is the witness's own unaided answer ("It would be exhibits..."). The retained list is COUNSEL'S recitation of the page, carried by a one-word "Correct." An interested party's reading of a document this library has never opened is reliable as to the words spoken, not as to what p. 8 says. The retained list is the weaker half and it is the half that the "re-testing is still possible" proposition rests on.

2. TWO NUMBERING SYSTEMS, IDENTICAL TOKENS. Oliver said "exhibits 1.4, 1.6, 1.9..." — but these are ATF laboratory item numbers, not court exhibits. Independently, Judge Graf's admitted-exhibit recitation on Day 4 reads: "I have State's Exhibit 1, 2, 3, 3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 5.1, 6, 6.1, 7, 7.1, 8, 8.1, 9, 10, 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, and I believe 12.4" (day4.txt 06:12:44, lines 5914–5922). The strings 3.1, 5.1, 7.1 and 8.1 exist in BOTH systems and mean different things. Any downstream use of "exhibit 5.1" is ambiguous unless the system is named. (The ATF reading is the correct one here: the court's list contains no 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 1.13, 2.1 or 4.1, and Oliver was reading p. 8 of her own report.)

3. MIXED POPULATION — "9 consumed vs 9 retained" is not like-for-like. The retained list includes 7.1 and 8.1, which are not evidence swabs: Day 4 reads a likelihood ratio referring to "Tyler Robinson, Exhibit 7.1" (day4.txt), i.e. 7.1 is a KNOWN/reference sample. Reference standards are routinely retained and are a different kind of thing from a scene or rifle swab. Strip them and the evidence-swab split is 9 consumed vs 7 retained, not 9 vs 9. A denominator swap waiting to happen.

4. SERIES GAP — 1.11 IS ON NEITHER LIST. `find(r'1\.11', 'day5.txt')` is a real null under BOTH the joined and hyphenated readings; the complete enumeration of `[1-9]\.\d{1,2}` tokens in day5.txt returns exactly the 18 designators of the two lists and nothing else. Yet 1.11 does exist — it appears twice in day4.txt. So the 1.x series runs 1.1–1.13 with 1.11 absent from p. 8. The transcript gives no reason. Scope of this null: day5.txt only; I did not attempt to establish what 1.11 is from Day 4, as that is outside this quantity.

5. NO 6.x ON EITHER LIST. `find(r'\b6\.1\b', 'day5.txt')` is a real null under both readings. An ATF item 6 may exist, may not have been DNA-tested, or may not exist at all — nothing on this record settles it. Anyone reading "2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1, 7.1, 8.1" as a contiguous series will silently invent a 6.1.

6. TWO LABS, TWO OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS OF "CONSUMED" — the sharpest break. At the ATF, "entirely consumed" (List 1) means nothing remains, and it is contrasted against items where "you consume the swabs, but you have some liquid extract remaining" (01:32:21/01:32:32). At the FBI, Bakker testified that items she calls CONSUMED still leave extract: "destructive testing is essentially consuming the sample; cutting the cotton off of the Q-tip or the swab, subjecting it to testing, so there's nothing remaining" (day2.txt 07:29:19), yet also "we do actually return the remaining extract, the liquid from our DNA testing. So we did consume the swab, however, there was a small amount of liquid that was left and returned" (day2.txt ~07:30). So an FBI "consumed" item is, in ATF vocabulary, an extract-retained item. The word cannot be pooled across the two labs, and a combined "N samples consumed" figure built from both would be wrong.

7. STOCK vs FLOW AT THE PAGE ITSELF. The retained list is phrased in the FUTURE tense on the face of the report — "you say the DNA extracts WILL BE retained" (01:31:51). That is a stated intention at report-writing time, not a verified present inventory. Nothing in this testimony establishes that the extracts still existed on July 13, 2026, or where they were. The consumed list, by contrast, is a completed-fact statement. Treating both as a single present-tense stock is a stock/flow error.

Residual scope — what I did NOT verify: I have not read p. 8 of State's Exhibit 30 (it is not among the 58 banked artifacts, so the entire figure is transcript-borne, T1-via-machine-transcript); I did not establish what ATF items 1.7, 1.8, 1.10, 1.12, 4.1 or 8.1 ARE; I did not search Day 4 for consumption statements about items outside Exhibit 30; and I did not check the certified transcript against the Rev machine transcript (standard Rev label-unreliability hazard applies — here the speaker labels at 01:31:35–01:32:14 are content-consistent, counsel asking and witness answering, so the attribution holds on its face).

results.finding:
Two ATF DNA (Forensic Biology) reports by ATF forensic biologist Laura Caitlin Oliver are in evidence, and they are the only ATF source of DNA likelihood ratios in the hearing record.

GROUP 1 — State's Exhibit 30 (ATF DNA report on the rifle, cartridge case and cartridges). Sgt. Faumuina identified it on Day 4 at 05:18:35: "This is the ATF report that I received regarding the DNA testing on the gun and cartridge and cartridge casings, oh, sorry, correction, cartridge case and cartridges." It contains exactly seven Statistical Analysis calculations covering ELEVEN ATF items, each with a stated ratio:
• Calc 1 — Exhibits 1.1 (stock and grips) + 1.4 (bolt): "The DNA profiles are at least one trillion times more likely if they originated from Tyler Robinson, Exhibit 7.1, as a contributor to the major components and three unrelated, unknown individuals than if they originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals." (Day 4, 05:21:57)
• Calc 2 — Exhibit 1.2 (butt plate): "at least one trillion times more likely ... as a major component and four unrelated, unknown individuals than ... five unrelated, unknown individuals." (Day 4, 05:22:33)
• Calc 3 — Exhibit 1.3 (trigger and trigger guard): "at least one trillion times more likely ... as a major component and three unrelated, unknown individuals than ... four" (Day 4, 05:23:05; re-stated by Oliver, Day 5, 02:14:27)
• Calc 4 — Exhibits 1.5 (fore-end) + 5.1 (one .30-06 cartridge): "at least one trillion times more likely ... as the major components and two unrelated, unknown individuals than ... three" (Day 4, 05:23:48)
• Calc 5 — Exhibits 1.6 (barrel) + 3.1 (one .30-06 cartridge): "at least one trillion times more likely ... as a contributor to the major components and two unrelated, unknown individuals than ... three" (Day 4, 05:24:24)
• Calc 6 — Exhibit 1.9 (optical accessory / scope): "The DNA profile is 6.28 billion times more likely if it originated from Tyler Robinson as a contributor to the major component and three unrelated, unknown individuals than if it originated from four unrelated, unknown individuals." results.breaks:
OBSERVED P8 BREAKS:

• CENSORED (CAPPED) VALUES PRESENTED AS MEASUREMENTS — the decisive one. Ten of the eleven Exhibit-30 ratios are not measured values but a floor: "the protocols in your laboratory say you cap that at the number one trillion. Is that right?" / Oliver: "Correct. We would not report a number higher than one trillion." (day5.txt 02:15:01). Only 1.9's 6.28 billion is an actual computed value. So "eleven items at one trillion or more" is ten identical ceiling-hits plus one real number; summing, averaging or ranking these is meaningless, and the closing's rhetorical expansion of the trillion ("replicating our world ... 120.48 times", final argument 06:22:25) treats a cap as a measurement.

• TWO OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS OF THE SAME STATISTIC. The ATF and FBI ratios are not on one scale. (a) Cap: ATF stops at 1 trillion; the FBI reports 1.7 octillion and 30 quintillion uncapped. (b) Propositions: ATF compares "Robinson + N unrelated unknowns" against "N+1 unrelated unknowns"; the FBI compares "Twiggs and T. Robinson" against "Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person" — Twiggs is carried in BOTH FBI propositions, so those ratios never test Twiggs's presence. (c) Verbal scale: the FBI attaches one ("very strong support for inclusion", day2.txt 07:18:42); ATF refuses one — "our laboratory doesn't use a verbal scale due to the fact that they add subjective words to the front of this word support" (day5.txt 01:24:09). Putting 1.7 octillion next to "at least one trillion" as though the first were 10^15 times stronger evidence is a definitional artefact.

• IDENTIFIER COLLISION / n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another. "Exhibit" means two different things in this record: State's Exhibit 30/31/33 are court exhibits, while 1.1, 7.1, 15.1, 18.1 are ATF laboratory item numbers also called "Exhibits" inside the report ("the report or the author refers to the items by their Exhibits numbers", day4.txt 05:20:17). Worse, ATF Exhibit 7.1/8.1 (Robinson's known sample and a second known) collide head-on with FBI Item 7.1/8.1 (towel swab, screwdriver swab). Any count that pools "7.1" and "8.1" across the two labs double-counts and mis-attributes.

• DENOMINATOR/POPULATION SWAP IN THE COUNT ITSELF. "Items with a likelihood ratio" varies by proposition-set: 11 Exhibit-30 items carry a Robinson-proposition ratio, but Oliver also calculated ratios on the same items for elimination-sample individuals — Matthew Robinson on 1.4 and 1.6, Lance Twiggs on the Dremel buttons and other Dremel areas — "there would have been a likelihood ratio statistic calculated and to go along with that" (day5.txt 01:50:08). Those exist on the record with no value attached, and only in a defence document.

• STATED vs EXISTING (the "stated" qualifier does real work). Exhibit 33 calculations 2–4 (items 15.3, 15.5, 15.6) carry paragraph-D ratios that were expressly left unread (day4.txt 05:34:45). 13 vs 16 is entirely this distinction; a count that does not say which convention it used is not reproducible.

• STOCK vs FLOW / SCOPE OF THE REPORT SET. Three ATF DNA reports by Oliver exist ("one report dated September 15, 2025, and two reports dated December 11, 2025", dc27998184), and she confirmed "all three of your reports" (day5.txt 01:24:49, 01:38:16, 01:43:09). Only two are identifiable as State's Exhibits. Any ATF ratio count from the hearing record is therefore a count over the reports IN EVIDENCE, not over the ATF's work in this case.

• ROUNDED FIGURES THAT NO LONGER SUM / UNIT INFLATION IN ARGUMENT. The closing's conversions — "an octillion is a 1 followed by 27 zeros. To get to an octillion, it requires 15 quadrillion trillions" (final argument 06:18:43) — do not reconcile: 10^27 is 1,000 quadrillion trillions (10^15 × 10^12), not 15. This is rhetoric in the recording layer, not a lab figure, but it is a stated arithmetic claim that fails.

RESIDUAL SCOPE (not re-verified): I did not open any ATF report PDF — no banked .txt or PDF in the artifacts folder carries the likelihood-ratio text (searched all 64 .txt artifacts under CR-ACQ-2026-07-27 for "likelihood rati", "times more likely", "quintillion", "octillion" via artifact_search.find, both joined and hyphenated readings: zero hits). So every ratio here is sworn testimony reading from an exhibit, not a direct read of the ATF report itself. The total number of statistical calculations in State's Exhibit 33 is not established by the record (at least five); the full item roster of Exhibit 33 and the identity of Oliver's third report are likewise unestablished. results.finding:
The examination was done by the FBI Laboratory's DNA Casework Unit, Quantico. The examiner is Amanda Bakker ("My name is Amanda Bakker. My last name is spelled B-A-K-K-E-R… I am a forensic examiner in the DNA Casework Unit of the FBI laboratory located in Quantico, Virginia," day2.txt 05:15:30–05:15:38), called out of order by the DEFENSE (Michael Burt) on Day 2 of the preliminary hearing. Her report is State's Exhibit 31, six pages; the towel result sits on page 3 of 6. The item is identified from the face of the report by SBI Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina: "Item 7, Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863" (05:08:38); the swabbing of it is Item 7-1.

PROFILE TYPE. Autosomal STR, developed with the FBI's GlobalFiler kit, and for the towel it was a FULL profile. Bakker: "at the FBI laboratory, we use a kit called GlobalFiler. And this is looking at 21 different locations on a human's DNA, in addition to three sex determining locations" (05:38:24); "A full profile means I have DNA at every single location. It is above our threshold and I'm seeing one or two pieces of information at each location. For item seven, I did develop a full profile" (05:40:26, line 6047). Male DNA was present, and the profile is a mixture, not single-source. The report language read into the record: "Male DNA was obtained from Item 7, sub 1" (05:10:57, line 4877). She also described "a slight amount of degradation, but not as much as Item 8" (05:34:57), which "did not" affect her conclusion (08:03:50). This is autosomal testing under the FBI's own "Approved Standards for Scientific Testimony and Reports for Autosomal DNA Testing" (05:22:10) and the DOJ "Uniform Language for Testimony and Reports for Forensic Autosomal DNA Examinations Using Probabilistic Genotyping Systems" (05:28:09). No Y-STR-only examination of the towel appears anywhere in the transcripts.

NUMBER OF CONTRIBUTORS. The reported figure is TWO — but the record carries a documented 3→2 amendment on this very sample, and that is the most important thing about the number. Reported: "Item 7, sub 1 was interpreted as originating from two individuals, one of whom is Twiggs" (05:10:57, line 4877). Originally, however, Bakker called three. Burt: "you originally determined in seven, sample seven, that there were three contributors" — Bakker: "That is correct, yes" (06:17:28–06:17:46, lines 7052–7053). Her technical reviewer (approval stamp: Tara Benson) had written the opposite: "she concluded that she would have called it a number of contributor of two. She compared it to my conclusions. I said number of contributor three. So we had a discussion as to why she thought it was two, why I thought it was three. And she said she agreed with me calling it three" (06:20:27, line 7140). The three-contributor call was made "somewhere around September 12th" (06:33:03) and changed "on September 13th of 2025" (06:33:30), for this reason: "I was submitted an elimination sample from Mr. Twiggs… When I compared him to this sample, all of the DNA, unlike that major contributor, matched to Mr. Twiggs. So because of that, I determined that there's actually only two individuals, because those small peaks, there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to" (06:33:52, line 7452). The number of contributors is her own input, not a software output: "NoC stands for Number of Contributors… That's my determination based on my experience and training looking at the data. That's something I input into STRmix" (05:59:16–05:59:30). The September 15, 2025 STRmix run for Item 7-1 was accordingly run on the two-person assumption — Burt: "you tell the software program, 'Assume there are two contributors,' right?" Bakker: "Correct, yes" (07:10:02–07:10:21, line 7801).

MIXTURE PROPORTIONS. Approximately 5% / 95%, and the examiner disclaims having calculated it herself. Burt: "did you determine what the proportion of mixture was between what I'll call the major contributor and the minor contributor?" Bakker: "I did not calculate that personally. Part of the STRmix software… During that process, it does give an estimate of the breakdown of those potential contributors" (05:53:41, line 6543). Burt: "for the seven sample, was the minor in there at less than 20% according to the STRmix?" Bakker: "Yes, it was. For one of the runs when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs, it was a 5% to 95%" (05:54:24, line 6551). So the towel's minor component is ~5% — below the 20% PCAST threshold Burt was pressing; her rebuttal was scope, not magnitude: "That is true, but in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals" (05:59:04).

WHOSE PROFILE ALIGNED WITH WHICH COMPONENT. Twiggs = the 5% minor; Robinson = the 95% major. Verbatim, on redirect by prosecutor Ryan McBride: Q — "Does that mean the 5% was from Twiggs and the 95%, that 95% is assumed from the defendant, Robinson?" A (Bakker, 08:05:58, line 9347) — "When I calculated the statistic, Twiggs' DNA profile aligned with the 5% contributor and Mr. Robinson's DNA profile aligned better with the 95% contributor." Note the asymmetry of status: Twiggs was treated as an ASSUMED contributor via an elimination sample supplied by investigators ("I talked to them with regards to if I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination versus comparing him and offering a statistic," 06:35:32), and Bakker resisted "source" language ("I don't want to use the word source," 06:36:07); Robinson is reported only as a POSSIBLE contributor, carried by the likelihood ratio. The LR, conditioned on Twiggs: "The DNA results from Item 7, sub 1 [are] 1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors" (05:10:57, line 4877). Under the DOJ directive the only permitted verbal equivalent is "very strong support for inclusion" (07:59:20–07:59:57).
results.value: Full autosomal STR profile (GlobalFiler), male DNA; 2 contributors interpreted (amended down from 3 on 2025-09-13); mixture ≈ 5% : 95%; Twiggs "aligned with the 5% contributor," Robinson "aligned better with the 95% contributor"; LR = 1.7 octillion
results.type: composite — count (number of contributors: 2, prior 3), share (mixture proportions: 5% / 95% of the DNA in the Item 7-1 extract), ratio (likelihood ratio 1.7 × 10^27), identifier (Item 7 / 7-1, State's Ex. 31 p.3 of 6)
results.unit: contributors = persons (count); mixture proportion = percent of DNA in the single Item 7-1 extract; likelihood ratio = dimensionless ratio of probabilities; loci = number of STR locations typed
results.denominator: Population = ONE DNA extract: Item 7-1, the swabbing from FBI Item 7, "Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863," recovered ~6:00 PM 2025-09-10 in the wooded area northeast of the Losee Center, UVU; collected by Utah SBI/State Crime Lab and released to FBI custody the same evening (Faumuina, 05:02:34–05:04:44). The 5%/95% shares are of the DNA in that one extract (sum = 100%). The likelihood-ratio denominator is the defense proposition: "Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors" — i.e. the LR is CONDITIONED on Twiggs being present, not computed against a two-unknowns alternative. Loci denominator: GlobalFiler, stated by the witness as 21 autosomal + 3 sex-determining = 24, but elsewhere as 23 (see breaks).
results.time_window: Evidence recovered 2025-09-10. Three-contributor interpretation "somewhere around September 12th" 2025; amended to two contributors "on September 13th of 2025"; STRmix run for Item 7-1 dated September 15, 2025; Bakker's reports dated September 15, 2025 and September 17, 2025 (Case ID SU-4130859, Lab Nos. 2025-01779-2 and 2025-01779-12, per the defense Touhy request filed 2026-04-02). results.comparator: Item 8, "Screwdriver from perch" — the paired item in the same report and the natural comparator. 1. n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another, on the headline count. The same extract was called 3 contributors, then 2, by the same examiner within 24 hours; her technical reviewer independently called 2, was talked up to 3, and the examiner then went back to 2 for a different reason. 3. Provenance/stock-vs-flow on the 5%/95%. It is NOT a reported figure from Exhibit 31. It is a by-product of one STRmix run — "I did not calculate that personally" (05:53:41) and "For ONE OF THE RUNS when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs" (05:54:24). Quoting it as "the mixture ratio of the towel swab" promotes a run-specific software estimate to a reported laboratory result.

4. Rounded figures that no longer sum (comparator item): 11% + 79% = 90% at 08:06:24, against 11% + 89% at 05:54:50. One of the two is wrong on the face of the record; I do not reconcile it.

5. Denominator/item swap hazard, live in this record. Item 7 = towel (5/95); Item 8 = screwdriver (11/89). The 08:05–08:06 redirect discusses 5/95 as "one of the samples" without naming it, immediately before the 11/79 answer — an easy path to attaching the wrong pair of percentages to the towel.

6. Two different operational definitions of "contributor" inside one report. Twiggs is reported as "a contributor" (assumed, via an elimination sample requested after the examiner spoke to investigators); Robinson is a "possible contributor" carried by an LR that is itself conditioned on Twiggs. Burt drew this out directly at 06:35:41–06:37:00 ("You don't say he's a possible contributor, like you do for Mr. Robinson, you say he IS a contributor"). "Aligned with the 5% contributor" is thus a conditioning assumption plus a visual peak comparison — at 07:21:11–07:21:25 Bakker confirms the Twiggs calculation was "uninformative" (LR of one) and that she did not use it: "I visually looked at the DNA sample." The 5% and 95% components are not two findings of the same kind.

7. Crude vs adjusted / scope-of-criterion mismatch on the 20% threshold. The towel's minor is 5%, below PCAST's 20%; Bakker's answer is that PCAST's concern was scoped to "mixtures of three or more individuals" (05:53:09, 05:59:04). Both statements are true and they are about different populations — citing either alone misstates the state of the record.

8. Loci-count inconsistency (24 vs 23) means "full profile" is defined against a denominator the witness stated two ways in the space of two minutes.

results.finding:
**Profile type.** Autosomal STR, and explicitly a PARTIAL profile. The FBI report (State's Exhibit 31), read into the record by Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina, says verbatim: "Item 8, Screwdriver from perch." (day2.txt 05:08:58) and for the sub-sample — which the prosecutor described as "swabs of the handle area of the screwdriver" (day2.txt 05:11:28, assented to) — "**Male DNA was obtained from Item 8, sub 1. Item 8, sub 1 was interpreted as originating from two individuals, one of whom is Twiggs. The DNA results from Item 8, sub 1 are 30 quintillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors, than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors.**" (day2.txt 05:11:41). The FBI examiner, Amanda Bakker (DNA Casework Unit, FBI Laboratory, Quantico), testified the kit was "a kit called GlobalFiler... looking at 21 different locations on a human's DNA, in addition to three sex determining locations" (05:38:24) — autosomal STR plus amelogenin, Y indel and DYS385 — and that the profile was incomplete: "**Item eight was a partial profile, so I did not develop DNA at every single location.**" (05:40:56), repeated as "**For item eight, I did not have a full profile, so I did not have data at all 23 locations to compare it to either Mr. Robinson or Mr. Twiggs.**" (05:41:59). She attributed this to degradation: "So Item 8 was the screwdriver from the perch. I would say that there was some degradation as I look at the DNA peaks or the DNA data... Here, I see a **ski slope-type effect**" (05:34:11), more degradation than Item 7, the towel (05:34:57). Interpretation was by probabilistic genotyping: "The software is called STRmix" (05:52:24).

**Number of contributors.** TWO, and two only, throughout. The report's own words: "originating from two individuals, one of whom is Twiggs" (05:11:41). Bakker's own rebuttal to the PCAST cross: "That is true, but in this case it was also **only a mixture of two individuals**." (05:59:04). The contributor number is her input, not the software's: "That's my determination based on my experience and training looking at the data. That's something I input into STRmix." (05:59:30). NOTE on a nearby trap I checked and am excluding: the 3→2 contributor revision (originally three on ~2025-09-12, changed to two on 2025-09-13 after Twiggs' elimination sample arrived — day2.txt 06:32:56–06:34:32) is tied on the record to the TOWEL, not the screwdriver: Burt asked of the technical reviewer's note page, "This is regarding the seven sample, correct?" and Bakker answered "That is correct. That is one of the samples." (06:12:23). No three-contributor history for Item 8 appears anywhere I searched.

**Mixture proportions — every figure on the record.** Only ONE source in the entire corpus states proportions for this item: Bakker's Day-2 testimony. Three statements, and they do not all agree.
(1) Bakker, on cross by Burt — "**For item eight, one of the contributors was 11% and the other was approximately 89%.**" (day2.txt 05:54:50). Note the hedge sits only on the larger figure.
(2) Provenance, given immediately before: "**I did not calculate that personally.** Part of the STRmix software... it takes a mixture and it uses math and biological modeling to try to break that mixture into its individual contributors... During that process, **it does give an estimate of the breakdown of those potential contributors**." (05:53:41). The proportions were never read from the FBI report; they are a STRmix output she was asked to recall.
(3) Prosecutor McBride's restatement on redirect — "I think you said the ratio was **11% from the minor and 89% from the major**. Is that Twiggs being the 11% and Robinson being the 89%?" (day2.txt 08:06:10).
(4) Bakker's answer to that question — "Yes. **Twiggs better aligned with that 11% contributor and Mr. Robinson better aligned with that 79% contributor.**" (day2.txt 08:06:24). This "79%" is the divergence; I am not reconciling it. It is in the Rev source HTML as well as the .txt.
The person↔proportion assignment is stated as alignment, not identity ("better aligned with"), and the parallel towel answer uses the same construction ("Twiggs' DNA profile aligned with the 5% contributor and Mr. Robinson's DNA profile aligned better with the 95% contributor," 08:05:58).
results.value: Partial autosomal STR profile (male DNA), TWO contributors, one of whom is Twiggs (an assumed/elimination contributor placed in both competing propositions); mixture proportions 11% / "approximately 89%" — minor 11% aligned with Twiggs, major 89% aligned with Robinson. A second statement of the same split gives the major as 79% (day2.txt 08:06:24). Associated likelihood ratio: 30 quintillion.

results.breaks:
OBSERVED (all verified in the primary transcript, not inferred):

1. **n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another / rounded figures that no longer sum.** The major contributor's share is 89% at day2.txt 05:54:50 and in the redirect question at 08:06:10, but **79%** in Bakker's answer at 08:06:24. 11+89=100; 11+79=90. The divergent figure is the LAST statement on the record and the one nearest a "yes," so any file quoting the closing exchange rather than the direct will carry 79%.

2. **Two operational definitions treated as one (the 20% comparison).** PCAST's threshold as read into the record is "at least 20% of the **intact DNA** in the mixture" (05:58:10) — a quantity-of-template measure. Bakker's 11% is a **STRmix estimate of contributor proportion** from the deconvolution (05:53:41), not a measure of intact DNA. The cross-examination compared them directly as if commensurable, and neither side stated the difference.

3. **Population/denominator swap in the comparator.** PCAST's stated scope is "mixtures of **three or more** individuals" with the minor at ≤20% (05:53:09). Item 8 is a **two-person** mixture. Burt's "both your samples had minor contributors below 20%" (05:58:58) is true of the number but applies a criterion defined on a population the sample is not in — which is precisely Bakker's rebuttal (05:59:04).

4. **Asymmetric scoping — run-specific vs unqualified.** The towel's 5%/95% is explicitly scoped: "for **one of the runs** when I compared to Mr. Robinson **conditioning on Mr. Twiggs**" (05:54:24). Item 8's 11%/89% carries NO run scope and no conditioning scope. This matters because Bakker testified STRmix is non-deterministic: "you will never get the same answer twice" (06:10:49), "each time you run the software, you will get a different number" (06:09:51). The screwdriver proportion is therefore a single-draw estimate presented without its draw.

5. **Denominator swap inside one exchange (loci).** 24 total loci (21 autosomal + 3 sex-determining) at 05:38:24/05:39:13 vs 23 at 05:40:10 and 05:41:59. The "partial profile" claim for Item 8 is stated against BOTH denominators, so the fraction of loci recovered cannot be rebuilt from this record at all — no numerator was ever given (she never said how many of the 23/24 loci produced data).

6. **Stock-vs-flow-adjacent provenance break: a figure attributed to a document it is not in.** The 11%/89% figures were never read from State's Exhibit 31. The report's own words for Item 8-1 state only the contributor count and the LR (05:11:41). The proportions came from Bakker's recollection of a STRmix output she says she "did not calculate... personally" (05:53:41). Any file marking 11%/89% as "the report's own words" mislabels testimony as document.

7. **Identifier collision — "Item 8" vs "Exhibit 8."** On redirect the prosecutor said item 7 had "slight degradation, not as much as **Exhibit 8**" (08:03:38), meaning FBI *item* 8; he self-corrected the same slip a minute later ("You testified about Exhibit 7 and 8... Excuse me. Yes, **items** seven and eight," 08:05:08). State's Exhibit 8 is a different thing entirely — a downward-pointing camera angle (2026-09-01_final-prelim-argument.txt ~04:39), and the screwdriver *photo* is State's Exhibit 3.1 (day1.txt 01:44:19), while the FBI *report* is State's Exhibit 31. Four distinct referents share the digits 3.1/8/31 in this record; a bare designator is not safe.

8. **A contributor assumed into both propositions.** The LR's competing propositions are "Twiggs and T. Robinson" vs "Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person" (05:11:41) — Twiggs is in BOTH, so the statistic never tested his presence; he entered as an elimination sample (06:33:52) after the contributor count had already been set at three and was then revised to two. Bakker declined the word "source" for him (06:36:07). This is a denominator/assumption break, not an arithmetic one, and it applies to the 11% figure as well since that 11% is the share attributed to the assumed contributor.

NOT OBSERVED: no calendar-vs-fiscal issue; no crude-vs-adjusted pairing; no stock-vs-flow confusion in the proportion itself.
