results.finding:
The two numbers have radically different evidentiary standing, and only one of them is rebuildable from a primary source.

THE LIMIT — 35 pages — IS PRIMARY AND VERBATIM. It was set orally by Judge Tony F. Graf Jr. at the close of Day 4 of the preliminary hearing (Day 4 = 2026-07-09; the 09-01 ruling states "a five-day preliminary hearing from July 6th to July 10th"). The colloquy, in order, from day1…day5 transcript file day4.txt:

Mr. Grunander (08:19:55): "Judge, page limits. We spoke as a team and our preference would be to limit at least the initial briefs on both sides to 30 pages, no longer than 30."
Ms. Visser (08:20:10): "I'd like to counter with 40."
Mr. Grunander (08:20:22): "We'll submit it, Judge. And then we would ask for half of whatever Your Honor grants for the final reply."
Judge Tony F Graf Jr (08:20:29): "All right. We will set it at 35 pages and then we will go half of that, which is an odd number. 17. We'll go 17 pages for the reply. The parties agree?"
Mr. McBride (08:20:45): "I was going to offer to round up to 18."
Judge Tony F Graf Jr (08:20:50): "All right. We will go with 18. So 35 pages for the initial filings, 18 response, and September 1st at 10:00 a.m."

So: 35 pages is the ceiling on each side's INITIAL brief (State's opening 07-28 and defence's 08-11 alike); 18 pages is the ceiling on the State's reply. The same colloquy fixed the 07-28 deadline — Grunander (08:17:54): "if we're able to collect the transcript Monday, if we had two weeks from Tuesday, we could have our motion in. I believe that's the 28th of July," and the Judge (08:18:05): "All right. So state's brief by the 28th of July, assuming that they can get the transcript by Monday."

THE FILING EVENT IS PRIMARY. From the bench, reading the bindover ruling, 2026-09-01: "The state filed its memorandum in support of a preliminary hearing bind over on July 28th, 2026. Defendant filed his preliminary hearing briefing on August 11th, 2026, and the state filed its reply memorandum on August 18th, 2026."

THE LENGTH — 28 pages — IS NOT REBUILDABLE FROM ANY PRIMARY SOURCE HELD HERE. The brief itself is held nowhere; it is the library's open acquisition item Q-45, and the banked State's reply of 2026-08-18 cites "the State's opening memorandum" four times without a single pin cite or page count. No transcript, no banked PDF, and none of the 33 banked outlet captures states a page count for it. The figure exists only in library restatements, and those restatements themselves disclose its provenance: it is the PAGE COUNT OF A SCRIBD LISTING for a third-party mirror upload, obtained by a summarising fetch that the library then declined to rely on. CR-WATCH-log.md, line 130 (Run 2, 2026-08-01): "A 28-page 'Memorandum in Support of Preliminary Hearing Bindover,' Case No. 251403576, is hosted on Scribd by The Post Millennial (HTTP 200, download offered)." And line 287 (Q-45 acquisition attempt, 2026-08-13), naming the channel: "A summarising fetch (the same channel class CR-E07 §1 logs as having fabricated a sentence that appears nowhere in the article it claimed to be reading) reached the Scribd page and returned its listing metadata — title as above, 28 pages, uploader The Post Millennial, a download button present."

WHICH IS WHICH — AND THE LIBRARY ALREADY KNEW THIS WAS THE TRAP. The conflation of these two numbers is a hazard the record flags in its own words, three times independently. CR-WATCH-log.md line 24 (Run 2 index row): "⚠ 28 pp. is the LENGTH; 35 was the page LIMIT." CR-WATCH-log.md line 259: "⚠ 28 pp. is the reported LENGTH of that brief. 35 was the court's page LIMIT. Do not conflate (Run 2's standing warning, restated because this is now the third file to touch the figure)." CR-WATCH-log.md line 1037 (v1.1 revision row) records that the conflation had actually occurred: "28 pp. is the actual length; 35 was the court's page LIMIT — the two were being conflated."

So the direction is: 28 = reported length (BELOW the ceiling), 35 = the ceiling. Any statement reversing these — calling the brief 35 pages, or the limit 28 — is wrong in both halves.

A FURTHER CAUTION THE SOURCES SUPPORT: even taken at face value, 28 and 35 are not commensurable, because they count different things. 28 is a PDF page count of a mirror upload; 35 is the court's ceiling on a filing's own pagination. The banked defence brief — the OTHER initial brief, under the identical 35-page limit — proves the gap is real and large on this very docket: it is 41 PDF pages, but its own arabic numbering runs 1–34 for the body (PDF pp. 7–40) with the certificate of service printed as "35" (PDF p. 41), behind an unnumbered caption page and five roman-numbered pages i–v. 41 PDF pages, 35 numbered pages, a 35-page limit. A "28 PDF pages" figure therefore cannot be compared to the 35 limit without knowing which convention it counts, and nothing in the record establishes that for the Scribd upload.

results.breaks:
OBSERVED, not hypothetical:

1. STOCK-VS-CEILING SWAP, the central break, and the record itself warns of it. 28 is a measurement of a document; 35 is a rule about documents. CR-WATCH-log.md line 1037 records that the two HAD ALREADY been conflated once ("the two were being conflated") and line 259 restates the warning "because this is now the third file to touch the figure." Reversing them, or reporting one where the other belongs, is the specific failure this quantity is exposed to.

2. TWO SOURCES, TWO OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS OF "PAGE" — and they demonstrably diverge by 6 on this docket. The 35 limit governs a filing's own pagination; the 28 is a PDF page count of a Scribd upload. The banked defence brief, under the identical limit, is 41 PDF pages but 35 numbered pages (unnumbered caption + i–v + body 1–34 + certificate "35"). If the Scribd mirror counts like the defence PDF, an underlying numbered length nearer 22 would produce "28 PDF pages" — the 28 cannot be laid against 35 as a like-for-like margin. Nothing in the record fixes which convention the 28 counts.

3. N-IN-ONE-PLACE ≠ N-IN-ANOTHER on the companion brief, with the direction reversed. State's reply: 19 PDF pages against an 18-page limit — over. Opening brief: 28 against 35 — under. CR-ACQ-2026-08-20_states-reply.md line 23 flags this explicitly and refuses to reconcile it: "19 vs 18 is recorded and deliberately NOT reconciled … same discipline as the 28-vs-35 hazard on the opening brief, but note the direction differs: there the number was below the limit." Whether a certificate-of-service page counts against a page limit is unresolved in this record, and it is the hinge for both comparisons.

4. INCONSISTENT PAGINATION CONVENTIONS BETWEEN THE TWO BANKED BRIEFS, which is why (2) and (3) bite. The defence brief has 6 pages of unnumbered/roman front matter before arabic "1"; the State's reply has none — its PDF page 18 carries printed "18" and PDF 19 carries "19", so PDF and printed counts coincide. Two filings, one cycle, one court, two counting bases.

5. A ROUNDED FIGURE THAT NO LONGER DERIVES FROM ITS RULE. The reply limit was defined as "half of whatever Your Honor grants" against a 35-page grant. Half of 35 is 17.5; the court said 17, then accepted a round-up to 18. 18 is therefore not half of 35 and cannot be re-derived from the 35 — anyone recomputing it will get 17 or 17.5 and conclude the record is wrong. It is not; the rounding is on the record at 08:20:45–08:20:50.

6. NUMERAL COLLISION ON "28" WITHIN THE LIBRARY. QUEUE.md line 221 (Q-98) describes the 2026-04-02 motion to vacate or continue as "(28 pp.)" — a different document, whose three banked PDFs are each 69 pages (pdfinfo, verified this pass). Any downstream search on "28 pp." in this corpus can land on the wrong filing. Also note 2026-07-28 is itself a date containing 28, adjacent to the page figure in nearly every sentence that carries it.

7. A PROVENANCE BREAK THAT SHOULD TRAVEL WITH THE NUMBER WHEREVER IT IS PRINTED. The 28 was returned by a summarising fetch that the library deliberately refused to treat as a reading of the document (CR-WATCH-log line 287 names the channel class as one that previously "fabricated a sentence that appears nowhere in the article it claimed to be reading"), and provenance on the mirror is expressly ZERO of three — no file-stamp, no signature block, no certificate of service ever rendered (CR-WATCH-log line 1035). The brief is Q-45, open since 2026-07-28 and "the only bindover-cycle document held nowhere." Reporting "28 pages" without that caveat states as a property of a court filing what is actually a property of an unverified third-party upload's listing page.

results.breaks:
P8 breaks actually observed:

1. **OPERATIONAL-DEFINITION SWAP (the significant one).** "Lines in the transcript" and "lines in the file" are different quantities here by 1,236 lines. The banked .txt files are full-page Rev.com scrapes: 203–204 lines of site navigation and marketing copy before the first word of testimony, and 44 lines of legal/marketing footer after the last. Any search-space or corpus-size claim resting on 35,743 is counting Rev's blog-category menu (including lines reading "Donald Trump", "Joe Biden", "Supreme Court", "Holidays") as part of the hearing record. The direction of the error is conservative for a null claim — a larger stated search space than the real one — but the stated number is not what it says it is.

2. **N-IN-ONE-PLACE ≠ N-IN-ANOTHER, from a counting convention.** `wc -l` counts newline characters; all five files end without one, so every per-file figure in the published 35,743 is short by exactly 1, and the total short by 5. The library's own line-range citations use sed/awk addressing, which DOES count that last line — so the same file is 9,640 lines long in CR-E19 §2 and addressable to line 9,641 in the citation convention used in CR-E06.

3. **UNIT SWAP (bytes labeled characters).** CR-E05 line 4 calls 327,506 the "characters" in day1.txt; that is `wc -c` (bytes). The character count is 327,480. Same shape as break 2: a tool's output adopted under the label a human would expect rather than the one the tool produces.

4. **THE UNIT IS NOT WHAT THE WORD IMPLIES.** "Transcript lines" normally means numbered court-reporter lines (~25/page). These are scraper wrap-points: each speaker attribution is split across three lines (name+"(", timestamp, "):"), and there are zero blank lines in any file. The count is a property of Rev's HTML-to-text extraction, not of any transcript, and would change on a re-fetch that rendered differently. It should never be cited as a measure of transcript length or converted to pages.

5. **POPULATION-BOUNDARY HAZARD (not an error, a trap).** The same folder holds a sixth transcript (`2026-09-01_final-prelim-argument.txt`, 1,438 lines) and four `*_condensed.txt` files. Observed, not hypothetical:
1. TWO OPERATIONAL DEFINITIONS OF THE SAME FIELD / n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another. FBI "Lab. "The ATF firearms report" is three documents (2025-09-17, 2025-10-06, 2026-02-25), two of them under the same submission 1. results.question_restated: At the 2026-09-01 hearing in State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson (Case No. 251403576, Fourth District Court, Provo), what date and time was the next setting fixed for; what alternative date was offered first; and what was said on the record about setting trial dates?
results.finding:
All three parts are established directly from the primary Rev transcript of the September 1, 2026 hearing; no evidence file was used.

**(1) The next setting fixed — October 23, 2026 at 1:00 PM, in person.** After bindover and arraignment were accomplished, Judge Tony Graf said at 08:43:08: "we will set this for a pretrial conference. And Counsel, given that we have bind over and the arraignment has been accomplished at the next hearing, I would like to set trial dates." He asked at 08:50:45: "What date do we have approximately 30 days out?" The setting was fixed at 08:55:53 — Graf: "All right, October 23rd at one o'clock here in person. And Defense, is it your request to have Mr. Robinson appear here in Court on that day?" — Novak: "Yes, Your Honor." — and restated at 08:56:07: "And Mr. Robinson, you'll join us on that date, **October 23rd at 1:00 PM**." The time was proposed by the court at 08:55:46 ("Absolutely. One o'clock?") after Novak asked at 08:55:24 for the afternoon so Burt could appear hybrid: "could we do the afternoon of the 23rd?" The court also reserved additional time that day — Speaker 12 (08:57:27): "That would be a window on the 23rd, Judge, of October," Graf (08:57:31): "So we can open up the rest of the day, essentially."

**(2) The alternative offered first — September 24, 2026, in the afternoon.** Clerk Trina (08:51:17): "The first date that we have available is going to be **September 24th in the afternoon**. The next date after that is October 23rd." Graf (08:51:35): "All right, September 24th or October 23rd. Looks like October 23rd is pretty open." September 24 was declined by the defense — Novak (08:51:50): "Your Honor, September 24th in the afternoon is definitely a problem for me, because the next morning at 9:00 AM I have to be in a federal courtroom in San Francisco. And Mr. Burt whispered to me that he's also not available on the 24th of September." (An earlier, partly inaudible mention of the same date is attributed to Kathy Nester at 08:44:44: "[inaudible 08:44:45] September 24th [inaudible 08:44:51]" — before the clerk read out the availability.)

**(3) Trial dates — discussed, requested, and NOT set on 2026-09-01.** The court deferred them to the October 23 setting (08:43:08, quoted above). The State said it would come ready to ask: Neiman (08:44:01): "We will be prepared when we appear next to the pretrial conference to ask for a trial setting and give the Court an idea of how long we think we'll need. We would like to come back as soon as possible for the next setting, as soon as two weeks, if the Court can accommodate that." Defense resisted a firm trial date: Nester (08:44:44): "So I would recommend maybe 30 days"; Novak (08:52:06): "we understand that late October is more than the 30 days, but I think it actually gives Counsel for Mr. Robinson and Counsel for the State the opportunity to really do our best to find common ground on a comprehensive, what I'm going to call pretrial litigation schedule with proposed deadlines for disclosures and the different litigation of the various issues. **Whether we can actually meaningfully identify a trial date at the end of that, I think is to be determined.**" Novak added (08:52:39): "I heard the State say they want to have trial next week, so they may have a trial date in mind, but we're just going to have to see what we can agree to and what we have to agree to disagree about." The victim-representative counsel closed by asking for a trial date on the 23rd — Neiman (08:56:32): "the two weeks have turned into seven weeks or six and a half weeks, whatever it is. We just ask that on the 23rd, a trial date be set, so that way at least the family knows that we have a trial date which we can gear towards… we would ask the Court, if possible, to please set the trial date on the 23rd of October." Graf replied only (08:56:57): "Thank you, Counsel. I appreciate you communicating your thoughts on behalf of the victim representative." **No trial date was set at the 2026-09-01 hearing.**

Supporting detail on why the 23rd nearly failed: Novak corrected himself at 08:52:59 — "Mr. Burt's unavailability is October 23rd because the Ninth Circuit has ordered him to appear for an oral argument"; Burt (08:53:54): "Any other date but the 23rd works." The court nonetheless kept the 23rd, accommodating Burt with an afternoon/hybrid setting after Novak conceded at 08:55:06: "we're going to go back to the date proposed by the Court in October."

results.breaks:
Observed P8 breaks:

**(a) Unit swap in the source cell itself — elapsed-recording time vs wall clock.** The Rev timestamps for this colloquy read 08:43–08:57, but the participants place it late in the day: Novak at 08:56:28 says "we appreciate the Court's time this **afternoon and this evening**," and Grunander's bindover argument sits at 06:25:38. The timestamps are offsets into the ~9-hour recording, not clock times. Anyone citing "08:51:17" as the moment the clerk offered September 24 would place an evening colloquy at 8:51 in the morning. The actual wall-clock time of the setting colloquy is not recoverable from this artifact.

**(b) Rounded figures that no longer reconcile.** "Roughly 30-day window" (court), "more than the 30 days" (defense), "seven weeks or six and a half weeks" (victim counsel) all describe the same 52-day interval. The 30-day framing was retained in the court's language at 08:53:20 even though the date already chosen was 52 days out.

**(c) Two operational definitions of the same event.** "Pretrial conference" (court) vs "status conference" (Novak, and Neiman once) for the identical 2026-10-23 1:00 PM setting — a definitional swap that would silently split this setting into two events in any downstream tally of hearings.

**(d) n-in-one-place ≠ n-in-another, via restatement.** The State's "two weeks" (to the next setting) becomes, in Novak's restatement, "trial next week." Setting-interval and trial-interval are different quantities; the record contains the conflation without correction.

**(e) Stock vs flow / requested vs fixed.** Three requested intervals are on the record (2 weeks, 30 days, "as soon as practically possible") and none is the interval fixed (52 days). A citation of "the parties agreed to ~30 days" would be false to the outcome; a citation of "the court set it 30 days out" would be false to the date.

**(f) Speaker-label defect (known project hazard, observed here).** At 08:55:50 the transcript labels "Michael Burt" as saying "That's okay with the State, Judge" — content identifies a prosecutor, not defense counsel Burt. The exchange at 08:55:46–08:55:53 (Graf "One o'clock?" → [label: Burt] "That's okay with the State, Judge" → [label: Novak] "That'll work?") is label-scrambled; the 1:00 PM time is nonetheless confirmed independently by Graf's own two restatements at 08:55:53 and 08:56:07, which is what I relied on. Also at 08:44:44 an "inaudible"-bracketed "September 24th" is attributed to Kathy Nester before the clerk read availability — treat that attribution as unreliable.

**(g) Calendar note (not a break, but a checkable anchor).** 2026-10-23 is a Friday and 2026-09-24 is a Thursday; both are plausible court days. 2026-09-01 + 30 days = 2026-10-01, which is not the date set.

Not observed: no fiscal-vs-calendar issue, no crude-vs-adjusted issue, no denominator swap (the quantity is a datetime, not a rate).
